text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Chancellor Helmut Kohl is confident Germany will keep its budget deficit to a 3.0 percent of gross domestic product limit required by the Maastricht treaty for joining European economic and monetary union. Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber thanked Kohl for his comments on this.
- Teachers in German regional state of Hesse protest against long work hours.
- The German government wants to convert old debts into euros, Europe's planned future currency, in 1999. Germany should remain the best debtor in the European Union
- Deutsche Telekom must offer access to its networks
- Wages below levels set in official pay agreements can be considered as profiteering, the Federal Court of Justice
HANDELSBLATT

- EU chief Jacques Santer says Germans are talking themselves out of the European currency union. Leading politicians abroad criticise the discussion in Germany about the euro. It does not inform citizens and makes them feel uneasy about the project.
- Low wages can be punished as profiteering, the Federal Court of Justice ruled
- IW German economic institute says no other industry work is more expensive than in western Germany. Institute says west Germany has the highest non-wage labour costs
- Defence Minister Volker Ruehe says cabinet will decide on financing of Eurofighter project on July 11
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber and Chancellor Helmut Kohl defuse the row over the euro. Bavaria's premier thanks Kohl for his remarks on keeping to the strict entry requirements for joining European economic and monetary union and for the timetable for its launch planned for 1999
- The number of ethnic German settlers in Germany from eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union has fallen considerably
- German Constitutional Court judges are too slow, the European Court of Justice says
- German economic institute says German non-wage labour costs are the highest in the world
DIE WELT

- EU partners criticise Germany's row over the euro. Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker and EU chief Jacques Santer are opposed to the Bonn criteria discussion. Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber meet in Munich
- Judges from European Court of Justice scold German constitutional court judges for taking too long to reach decisions
- Eurofighter fighter jet project is being included in the budget
- West German workers are the most expensive in the world, economic institute said non-wage labour costs are highest
- Trade union protests against government's health reform.
